title: Where GitHub Copilot Actually Saves Time in AL Projects
summary: GitHub Copilot saves time in AL development through deliberate use of Chat, Agent, Ask, and Edit modes for specific tasks. Agent mode generates boilerplate and test scaffolding efficiently, Chat mode helps explore unfamiliar APIs, Ask mode explains existing code, and Edit mode refactors with precision, though all generated code requires developer review before acceptance.
key_points: Agent mode efficiently generates AL boilerplate code and test scaffolding when given clear intent descriptions
Chat mode provides quick working examples for exploring unfamiliar APIs like HttpClient and JSON handling
Ask mode helps developers understand existing code by identifying responsibilities, table interactions, and design characteristics
Edit mode enables precise, reviewable refactoring by extracting logic into separate procedures
Generated code is structurally correct but occasionally contains syntax errors requiring developer verification before acceptance
features: Copilot Agent mode for code generation
Copilot Chat mode for API exploration
Copilot Ask mode for code explanation

quotes.text: The key is using the right mode for the right task.
quotes.why_it_matters: Copilot productivity depends on matching its mode to the specific development task, not treating it as a generic autocomplete tool

quotes.text: The quality of what Agent produces is directly proportional to the clarity of the intent you give it.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clear problem definition before requesting code generation is essential for obtaining production-ready output
